Those four ordinary/reviewed and full/result-only selections reproduce complete packages from two author roots, install offline after author removal and replay the C11/GMP caller unchanged after physical relocation. Invalid graphs preserve caller data and the initialized output before a later valid call proves recovery. The local runs used Linux x64/glibc 2.36 and do not establish execution at the glibc 2.38 release floor. The [recurring workflow](https://github.com/seanmorris/lean-bridge/actions/workflows/nested-checked-record-native.yml) requires the same four selections at that floor. [Inherited checked-record acceptance](../evidence/inherited-checked-record-promotion-20261018.md) separately covers the tested proof-free `Span → Ticket → Stamped` chain.

The [hosted zero-payload archive](../evidence/zero-payload-checked-record-native-20261021.md) covers proof-only `Witness`, Unit-bearing `Token`, plain empty `Marker`, options, arrays and active/inactive variant branches at copied parameters and results. `Witness` uses a named generated structure with one non-semantic `uint8_t` storage byte because C structures cannot have zero size. That byte is not a Lean field or proof. Full packages run the selected nullary Lean constructor, preserve rejected inputs and recover; result-only packages return the same proof-erased carriers without input-constructor metadata. The run passed on glibc 2.39 with a glibc 2.38 package floor.

Generic checked records, value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, other index kinds, open dependent records, zero-payload fields and callbacks, owned positions and other zero-payload shapes remain unreviewed.

[Zero-payload checked records in C and C++](zero-payload-checked-record-native-20261021.md)
record four hosted native package selections for proof-only `Witness`,
Unit-bearing `Token`, plain empty `Marker`, Option, Array and variant values.
- [Zero-payload checked records in C and C++, 21 October 2026](zero-payload-checked-record-native-20261021.md)

#### Export a proof-only checked record

A proof-only record is a real nominal value, not `Unit`, null or absence. Declare the structure in `Type`, provide a nullary checked constructor such as `def mkWitness : Option Witness`, and select that constructor at each public input site. The host receives an empty carrier; a record with a `Unit` field keeps that field. Lean-produced results need no input constructor.

The [hosted C/C++ zero-payload archive](../evidence/zero-payload-checked-record-native-20261021.md) validates proof-only `Witness`, Unit-bearing `Token`, plain empty `Marker`, options, arrays and variant branches through ordinary and reviewed full/result-only packages. C uses a single non-semantic byte to give the nominal structure legal storage; C++ uses an empty structure. Neither carrier contains a proof.

For a record whose proofs relate its fields, use a [checked constructor over the payload fields](existing-package.md#export-a-record-with-proof-fields). The host supplies no proof. The compiler checks each input through the selected Lean constructor and erases proofs from Lean-produced results. Closed `Nat`, `Bool`, and `String` indices stay in authenticated type metadata and never become host fields; the [complete hosted value-index matrix](../evidence/checked-record-value-index-matrix-promotion-20261020.md) exercises all three closed forms at top-level copied checked-record parameters and results in all 17 consumer profiles. Top-level inputs and results have installed acceptance in C/C++, Node JavaScript/TypeScript, browser pages, React, workers, Python, Rust, Ruby, .NET, Java/Kotlin, Perl, native PHP, PHP-Wasm and WIT/WASI. npm has [installed nested acceptance](../evidence/nested-checked-record-browser-20261016/index.json), C/C++ have an [installed nested archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-native-20261016/index.json), .NET has an [installed NuGet archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-dotnet-20261016/index.json), Java/Kotlin have an [installed Maven archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-jvm-20261016/index.json), Perl has an [installed CPAN archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-perl-20261016/index.json), native PHP has an [installed Composer archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-20261016/index.json), Python has an [installed wheel archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-python-20261016/index.json), Ruby has an [installed gem archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-ruby-20261016/index.json), WIT/WASI has an [installed component archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-wit-20261016/index.json), PHP-Wasm has an [installed Node/Chromium archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-wasm-20261016/index.json), and Rust has an [installed Cargo archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-rust-20261016/index.json). They cover direct and repeated parameters, arrays, lists, options, products, `Except`/`Result`, enclosing record fields, active variant fields and constructor-free container results. [Installed inherited checked-record acceptance](../evidence/inherited-checked-record-promotion-20261018.md) additionally covers the tested acyclic `Span → Ticket → Stamped` chain, with independently selected parent and child constructors and proof-free results. Select the record constructor and each nested checked field's constructor independently at every public input site; only an active variant branch runs. A record whose only fields are proofs is still a checked record: declare it with an explicit `: Type`, select a nullary constructor such as `def mkWitness : Option Witness`, and the host passes and receives an empty carrier that is distinct from an absent, null or default value; a record with one `Unit` field beside its proofs keeps that field. The [hosted C/C++ zero-payload archive](../evidence/zero-payload-checked-record-native-20261021.md) validates that boundary through options, arrays and active/inactive variants in ordinary and reviewed full/result-only packages. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results. Standalone result-only packages expose the same results without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal empty carrier; C uses one non-semantic uint8_t storage byte solely to give the structure a legal nonzero size, while C++ uses an empty structure. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains an ordinary empty record, and Option presence, arrays, and the active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata."

The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results. Standalone result-only packages expose the same results without checked-input metadata. Proof-only Witness crosses as a nominal empty carrier; C uses one non-semantic uint8_t storage byte solely to give the structure a legal nonzero size, while C++ uses an empty structure. Token keeps its Unit field, plain empty Marker remains an ordinary empty record, and Option presence, arrays, and the active or inactive Mark branches remain distinct. Full packages validate nullary checked constructors and exact rejection and recovery. Result-only packages project Lean-produced proof-erased values without input-constructor metadata."

The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as ordinary GMP integers in C and cpp_int values in C++. The generated adapter applies the exact constructor selected for Packet and its nested Word field through direct and repeated parameters, Array, List, Option, Product, Except, Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value branch. C callers initialize and clear generated records and owning results; C++ callers use Packet values, vectors, optionals, products, results, Holder and Choice. Rejected inputs leave the complete caller graph and existing C output unchanged, and later valid calls recover. Array and Option results contain proof-free Packet payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results.
